thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • Severity S2 • Cross-region routing anomaly detected for eu-west users. Alert: increased p50/p95 latency to 2-4s and 5xx spike ~2.3% from 09:12 UTC. Auto-detection rule: geo-route-telemetry-guard.

sarah (oncall): saw the pager, reassigning to me. pinging networking.

sarah (oncall): @raj can you join? i'm collecting traces now.

raj (networking): on it. initial check: traffic funneling to apac-edge-03 for some eu-west client IP ranges. weird — routing policy shows eu->eu pinned routes, but some prefixes match fallback set.

dave (infra): tagging along. any DNS anomalies? i'm seeing DNS TTL still 300 on geo pin records but some caches returning apac records.

lina (prod-sre): quick check: error rate mostly 502/504 from gateway layer, upstream latency to apac region high. user impact: chat generation requests timing out for a subset of customers in EU.

emily (support): we already have 5 tickets in queue, customers reporting slow responses. putting a status note draft in product-status (no public yet).

sarah (oncall): timeline so far — alert at 09:12, confirmed routing mismatch at 09:16. Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily force-route eu traffic to eu-primary (pin-override), 2) flush problematic DNS cache / reduce TTL, 3) open ticket with cloud provider for inter-region steering bug. actioning 1 now.

raj (networking): running command: `rlsctl route override --scope=eu --target=eu-primary --reason=\"pin drift mitigation\"`

incident-bot: ACTION_STARTED by raj at 09:20 UTC — route override in progress.

dave (infra): applying DNS short TTL patch: `dnsctl set-ttl geo-eu 60` and `dnsctl flush cache --regions=public-resolvers` — running now.

sarah (oncall): applying canary to 10% first to watch for regressions.

raj (networking): canary engaged. traffic shift 10% -> eu-primary. watching telemetry.

lina (prod-sre): p50 down from 2.8s to 1.1s in canary, error rate on canary is nominal. good sign.

emily (support): started notifying affected customers in queue that we're working on routing fix, ETA 30-60m.

sarah (oncall): ramping to 100% override now. `rlsctl route override --scope=eu --target=eu-primary --force --sync`

incident-bot: ACTION_COMPLETED by raj at 09:33 UTC — override applied globally for EU region.

dave (infra): DNS TTL change propagated to many resolvers; some public caches still holding old records — TTL flush request has been sent to CDN/network provider.

lina (prod-sre): post-override telemetry: p95 dropped from 4.1s -> 0.9s, 5xx down to 0.2%. Customer impact largely mitigated. continuing to monitor for reappearance.

raj (networking): root cause hypothesis: routing policy evaluator had a regex ordering regression causing some prefix matches to fall through to global fallback that routes to APAC. Pinning metadata didn't block fallthrough in certain overlapping prefix sets. filing bug: RG-1984.

sarah (oncall): classification: cross-region policy misroute due to evaluator-rules priority bug -> caused eu pins to be bypassed for ~12% of affected prefixes. Duration of impact ~ 21 minutes (09:12 - 09:33) for most users; residual DNS cache tail extended to ~45 minutes in edge caches.

emily (support): impacted customers list: customer A (EU), customer B (EU), and a handful of enterprise eval instances. drafting outreach note with timeline and mitigation steps.

lina (prod-sre): impact estimate: ~1.9% of total EU requests saw errors/timeouts, severity set S2 because partial degradation and some enterprise user impact.

raj (networking): workaround committed to stable: add explicit prefix-exact rule ordering and a safety-check to ensure pin set overrides fallthrough. rolling PR to prod later today.

dave (infra): creating remediation tasks: 1) full rollout of evaluator fix, 2) add synthetic probes that verify region pinning per-prefix, 3) telemetry alert tuning to catch prefix-fallthrough earlier.

sarah (oncall): handoff plan: i'll be on for 30 more minutes to observe, then handing to raj for follow-up remediation and to lina for post-incident monitoring.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF scheduled at 10:05 UTC — from sarah to raj.

raj (networking): acknowledged handoff. i'll own the bug ticket and coordinate PR/release. timeline target: PR review + staged rollout within 6 hours.

lina (prod-sre): i'll keep the dashboard/alerting watch for next 24 hours. will add a temporary dashboard tile showing per-prefix pin drift.

emily (support): will send customer follow-ups after we confirm the PR plan. draft shared in #support-drafts for review.

sarah (oncall): closing incident thread for active mitigation. please post updates here as remediation progresses. thumbs if you saw. :thumbsup:

raj (networking): thumbs. filing RG-1984 now with logs and sample prefixes + link to this thread.

lina (prod-sre): note for postmortem: include timeline, DNS cache tail analysis, and invite infra/networking/product.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) • Resolved state at 09:40 UTC • Severity downgraded to S3 for follow-up.

sarah (oncall): final note: immediate customer-facing impact mitigated by route override; residual risk from public DNS caches handled via TTL flush and provider ticket. we'll run post-incident review tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

emily (support): thanks team — prepping customer emails and incident summary for stakeholders.

(reacts: several :eyes:, :thumbsup:)
metadata_note: This thread documents live mitigation steps, on-call handoff, customer impact, and initial root cause hypothesis for a cross-region routing/pin drift incident.
